A. The relationship between doctor and client is confidential and therefore, access to a patient’s medical records shall be limited only to that information necessary to complete basic police functions.
p
B. Officers should be mindful that it is only the responsibility of medical personnel to provide police officers only those records necessary for the completion of police functions.
p

C. Medical personnel cannot, at the expense of jeopardizing the patient’s physical and mental well-being, permit any form of interviewing without the attending physician’s concurrence. No interview shall take place until permission is granted.
p

D. Persons in police custody brought to the emergency room for examination and treatment shall not be left unattended by police officers during the course of their stay. It is necessary that a police guard be present at all times to assure the safety of not only the person in custody, but other patients, visitors, and employees as well.
p

E. When a person arrested by patrol needs to be transported from the jail to the hospital for examination and treatment, the arresting division will be responsible for the transport and the guard duty. In the event the transport need is immediate, Central Division will initiate the transport while dispatch immediately sends the first available unit from the arresting division to relieve the Central Division transport unit. Dispatch has the discretion to send any available unit to initiate the transport if no Central Division units are available or one is closer to the jail.
p

F. When a person arrested by a specialized unit needs to be transported from the jail to the hospital for examination and treatment, the specialized unit will be responsible for the transport and guard duty if that specialized unit is on-duty, uniformed, and equipped for prisoner transport. If the arresting specialized unit is not available, dispatch will start a city‐ wide rotation for guard duty until the arresting specialized unit is available and that unit meets the previous listed criteria. The city‐wide guard duty will begin with the division in which the arrest occurred. In the event the transport need is immediate, Central Division will initiate the transport while dispatch immediately sends the first available unit from the division in which the arrest occurred to relieve the Central Division transport unit. Dispatch has the discretion to send any available unit to initiate the transport if no Central Division units are available or one is closer to the jail.
p
G. When relieving an officer on guard detail, the relieving officer shall be advised of the charges and other pertinent information regarding the patient by the officer being relieved.
p
H. Persons in police custody shall not be allowed visitors without the approval of the investigative supervisor with jurisdiction over the case.
p
I. When notified of a person’s pending release from a hospital or other agency, the officer shall contact the jail supervisor for guidance on the disposition of the person.
p
J. This policy is not intended to be approval for overtime. Each supervisor is responsible for ensuring that proper relief is found for units that reach the end of their shift on a guard detail.
